newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Securitas joins move to Stockholm O-list.
newsitem.headline: Securitas joins move to Stockholm O-list.

text.p: Swedish security company Securitas said on Tuesday that it had decided to move to the Stockholm bourse's smaller O-list from the A-list.
Securitas is the latest in a long list of Swedish companies to move lists to avoid a new wealth tax. Companies listed on the O-list are exempt from the tax.

The law has caused companies like fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, media group Marieberg, construction group Lundbergs and investment companies Latour and Custos to flee from the A to the O list since June.
A 1996 law forces Swedes with wealth exceeding 900,000 crowns to pay 1.5 percent tax on 100 percent of the value of shares listed on the A-list.

But the recent share transfers were triggered by a law adopted by parliament in June reaffirming that main shareholders in companies have to pay tax for shares listed on the A list before 1991. Companies had hoped parliament would change the 1996 law.
Securitas said in a statement that the move would take effect from July 23.
